title: Runtime Playground Operator Handbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This handbook documents the operator workflows, safety gates, telemetry contracts, and procedural recipes for running the Runtime Playground — a curated staging cluster where runtime, kernel, and scheduler experiments are carried out end-to-end. The Playground is the canonical environment for: kernel prototype rollouts, scheduling-policy stress tests, profiling and latency-attribution experiments, and candidate benchmarking suites prior to canarying into production.

Goals
- Provide a low-friction but safe path to run destructive/performance experiments.
- Preserve fidelity to production execution surfaces while isolating blast radius.
- Ensure experiments produce reproducible artifacts (traces, tracesets, golden benchmarks).
- Make rollbacks and postmortems fast and deterministic.

Audience
- Runtime engineers implementing kernel or scheduler changes.
- SREs validating capacity/eviction behaviors.
- Applied ML engineers testing model-variant cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Performance engineers authoring benchmarks and profiling harnesses.

Key Concepts
- Playground Cluster: A dedicated tenant-aware runtime cluster with production-like GPUs, reduced traffic, and explicit circuit breakers.
- Shadow Traffic: Mirrored production request surface used for fidelity tests without impacting users.
- Decision Trace: A serialized, linkable trace that captures routing and scheduler decisions for every experimental run.
- Fidelity Gate: A quality threshold (latency/cost/quality) that must be met for an experiment to advance.

Ownership and Contacts
| Role | Team | On-call / Primary | Escalation |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Playground Owner | Eng - Serving Runtime | Jonah Kim | Pager: eng-runtime-oncall |
| Kernel Sandbox Custodian | Eng - Kernel | Marta Alvarez | Slack: #kernel-sandbox |
| Observability Lead | Eng - Platform | Ethan Zhou | Pager: observability-oncall |

Environment Layout
- Cluster name: playground-us-west-2 (k8s namespace: playground-runtime)
- GPU mix: 8x A10G (evaluation), 4x H100 (reserved testbeds)
- Network: Isolated VPC with egress-only to infra systems (S3, telemetry-api)
- Data retention: experiment artifacts stored 30 days by default; long-term artifacts archived to experiments-bucket with TTL policy.

Pre-flight Checklist (must be green before any experiment)
1. Create an Experiment Issue and link to this handbook (template: EXP-PLAYGROUND).
2. Confirm resource quotas with Capacity Owner (Slack: #capacity).
3. Confirm tracking keys for telemetry: experiment_id, run_id, operator, hypothesis.
4. Smoke test baseline traces: run 100 requests of the target profile and capture Decision Traces.
5. Ensure canary circuit breaker flags are configured: playground.allow-destructive (bool), playground-kernel-override (list).

Experiment Lifecycle
1) Plan
- Hypothesis: short phrase describing expected change (e.g., "sharded attention reduces p95 by >= 8ms for seq=1024").
- Metrics: primary (p50/p95 latency), secondary (token throughput, kernel queue length), safety (error rate, OOM count).
- Acceptance criteria: numeric thresholds and max allowed regressions.

2) Authoring
- Add experiment config (YAML) to experiments/ directory in git. Example: 

```yaml
experiment_id: exp-2025-4623
description: "priority-aware kernel sharding test"
variants:
  - name: control
    kernel_profile: v2
  - name: shard-12
    kernel_profile: v3-sharded
traffic: shadow-mirror
traffic_weight: 0.0 # mirrored only
duration: 2h
telemetry: decision-trace,perf-sample,kvcache-dump
rollback_on:
  - error_rate > 0.5%
  - p95_control - p95_variant > 10ms
```

3) Scheduling and Execution
- Submit experiment via cli: `rk experiment submit --file exp-2025-4623.yaml --owner asha.patel`
- The scheduler assigns to a sandboxed node group with admission-controller policy applied.
- Use `rk experiment status <id>` to follow progress.

4) Profiling and Data Capture
- Enable continuous profiler snapshot: `rk profiler start --experiment <id> --sample-rate 1/1000`
- For kernel-level traces enable kernel-hint logging: set KGLOG=debug in experiment env.
- Ensure prefix/KVcache dumps are captured at run start and end: `rk kvcache dump --experiment <id> --bucket experiments-bucket`

5) Analysis and Artifact Collection
- Golden artifacts to collect: Decision Traces (JSON), perf-samples (parquet), microbench histograms (txt), kernel logs (tar.gz).
- Use artifact aggregation script: `scripts/collect_artifacts.sh <experiment_id> > artifacts/<experiment_id>.tar.gz`
- Run bench-compare tool: `bench-compare --left=control --right=shard-12 --metrics=p95,p50,tokens/s --output=reports/<id>.html`

6) Post-run Review and Gates
- Populate the experiment issue with: summary, artifacts link, pass/fail against acceptance criteria, and next steps.
- If gates fail, tag `regression` and assign to owner. For failures with unknown root cause, follow the Incident Triage Runbook (section below).

Safety and Blast Radius Controls
- Admission policies: no experiment may allocate > 30% of a sandbox node group's memory or > 50% of GPU cycle credits.
- Circuit breakers: automatic abort on sustained OOM > 3 within 10 minutes or kernel panic observed.
- Network egress: disallowed to customer endpoints; only infra endpoints permitted.
- Identity: experiments run under a limited service account with no access to production secrets.

SLOs and Monitoring for Playground
- Uptime: 99.5% cluster level for experimental scheduling controller.
- Telemetry latency: Decision Trace publish latency < 30s 95th percentile.
- Artifact availability: experiment artifacts available for download within 5 minutes of run completion.

Runbook: Incident Triage for Regressions in Playground
1. Detect
  a. Alert triggers: bench-compare flags p95 regression > acceptance threshold; profiler shows CPU or kernel queue saturation; artifact pipeline fails.
2. Contain
  a. Stop the experiment: `rk experiment abort <id>` (immediate).
  b. Quarantine node(s): mark nodes unschedulable and collect kernel-state snapshot.
3. Diagnose
  a. Pull Decision Traces: `rk trace fetch --id <run_trace_id>` and open in Trace Viewer.
  b. Correlate perf-samples with kernel logs (time-aligned).
  c. If OOM suspected, run `rk memory-audit --node <node> --since <ts>` to get allocation flamegraphs.
4. Remediate
  a. If regression is kernel-level, revert kernel candidate using `rk kernel rollback --name <candidate>` and re-run smoke-tests.
  b. If scheduling policy error, restore previous scheduler policy from policy-store tag `stable`.
5. Postmortem
  a. Create a postmortem document with links to artifacts and hypothesis tests.
  b. Run a mini-experiment that increments in smaller steps to validate fix.

Benchmarks and Reproducibility
- Benchmark templates live in `benchmarks/templates/` and must declare: workload profile (concurrency, sequence distribution), model variant, kernel hints, and warmup protocol.
- Reproducibility note: always seed the request generator and record seed in Decision Traces.

Kernel and Scheduler Experiment Patterns
- Priority Staircase Test: Verify priority decoupling by stepping traffic through priority buckets (0->1->2) and measuring cross-priority interference.
- Sharded-KV Warmup Pattern: Pre-warm KV shards deterministically using synthetic prefix sequences to avoid cold-start noise.
- Kernel Hedging Probe: Inject low-latency hedged kernel calls to test preemption and cooperative handoff.

Example Kernel Rollback Command (safe pattern)

```bash
# verify artifacts before rollback
rk kernel candidate inspect --name v3-sharded --artifacts \
  --expect-files kernel.so,kernel-meta.json
# promote previous stable
rk kernel promote --from-tag stable --to active --confirm
# monitor health
rk health watch --filter kernel,eviction,oom --duration 10m
```

Release Notes and Change Log (playground-specific)
- 2024-11-12: Initial handbook and cluster provisioning template.
- 2025-01-18: Added automated decision-trace enrichment and bench-compare output format.
- 2025-02-03: Updated safety thresholds for GPU credit usage and artifact TTL policy.

Common Known Issues (Playground)
- Artifact pipeline stalls when S3 throttling observed: mitigation — reduce parallel uploads and add exponential backoff (see scripts/collect_artifacts.sh).
- Kernel candidate fails with assert in `kv_shard_indexer`: usually due to mismatched shard map; mitigation — run `rk kvcache validate --map` then replay warmup.
- Shadow traffic skew: if production sampling is not representative, use synthetic traffic generator with recorded seed and distribution to improve fidelity.

Appendices
A. Experiment Issue Template (EXP-PLAYGROUND)
- Title, hypothesis, acceptance criteria, duration, resource request, telemetry keys, owner, reviewers.

B. Artifact Naming Convention
- `<experiment_id>.<run_id>.decision-trace.json`
- `<experiment_id>.<run_id>.perf-samples.parquet`
- `<experiment_id>.<run_id>.kvcache.tar.gz`

C. Quick CLI Cheat Sheet
- `rk experiment submit --file <yaml>` — submit an experiment.
- `rk experiment status <id>` — status.
- `rk experiment abort <id>` — abort.
- `rk profiler start --experiment <id>` — enable continuous profiler.
- `rk trace fetch --id <trace_id>` — fetch decision trace.

D. Post-experiment Retention Policy
- Short-term: artifacts retained 30 days.
- Long-term: curated artifact sets (postmortem-critical) archived for 365 days.

E. Related Playbooks
- runtime-upgrade-validation-and-canary-matrix-2026 (for production rollout)
- kernel-handshake-and-adaptive-fallback-patterns-2026 (kernel-level behavior reference)

If you have questions or an experiment need, open an EXP-PLAYGROUND issue and tag @playground-ops.
